fixes.explanation: Close, friend, but this one's not an altar. Verse 2 says David and his troops set out to bring up the ark of God from Baale of Judah. Thirty thousand chosen men, one errand, and it's the ark. I once hauled a single cooling rack across my bakery and needed a sit-down after.
No crown on this errand, friend. Verse 2 says David and his troops set out to bring up the ark of God from Baale of Judah. That's the whole mission. Nobody packed a crown for this trip.

Yes! Verse 5 says David and all the house of Israel were celebrating before the LORD with all kinds of wood instruments, harps, stringed instruments, tambourines, sistrums and cymbals. That's a full band on the road. I can't even get my mixer and my timer to keep the same beat.

That's what verse 7 says. The anger of the LORD burned against Uzzah, and God struck him down on the spot. He died there beside the ark of God. Uzzah was one of the sons of Abinadab who were guiding the new cart (verse 3). This part is heavy.

That isn't what happens here. Verse 7 says God struck Uzzah down on the spot, and he died there beside the ark of God. The text doesn't mention his hand. Uzzah had reached out and taken hold of the ark because the oxen had stumbled (verse 6). This part is heavy.

Uzzah isn't sent anywhere. Verse 7 says God struck him down on the spot, and he died there beside the ark of God. He had reached out and taken hold of the ark because the oxen had stumbled (verse 6). This part is heavy.

Yes, irreverence. Verse 7 says God struck him down on the spot for his irreverence. That's the word the text gives for it. Verse 6 tells us what Uzzah did: he reached out and took hold of the ark of God.

Laziness never comes up here. Verse 7 says God struck Uzzah down on the spot for his irreverence. That's the reason the text gives. Verse 6 says what he did: he reached out and took hold of the ark of God.

No sickness in this verse. Verse 11 says the LORD blessed Obed-edom and all his household while the ark stayed there three months. The text only tells us about blessing. I think the folks in that house were glad to have that news go around.

That's it, friend! Verse 12 says David went and had the ark of God brought up from the house of Obed-edom into the City of David with rejoicing. A report comes in, and David gets moving. And look at that last word: rejoicing. The trip is a lot happier than it was the first time!

Quiet? Not even close, friend! Verse 14 says David danced with all his might before the LORD. Then verse 15 says he and all the house of Israel brought up the ark with shouting and the sounding of the ram's horn. Dancing, shouting AND a ram's horn. Nobody was tiptoeing anywhere.

That's not what David says. He says, “I will celebrate before the LORD, and I will humiliate and humble myself even more than this.” He doesn't mention keeping it private. He says he'll celebrate before the LORD and go even further.
